subject: Operational signals + smoke-test suite for MAP (draft)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen@medswift.com>, procurement@medswift.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Operational signals + smoke-test suite for MAP (draft)

Hi Helen / MedSwift team,

Appreciate the time on the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a working draft of the MAP operational signals and a short smoke-test suite that we plan to run during the 2-week pilot. High-level goals: drive clarity on what "pass" looks like, who owns each check, and what the go/no-go exit gates are.

Key pieces in this draft (attached: MAP_operational_signals_v1.xlsx; smoke_test_scenarios.md):
- Success signals: throughput, latency, core-concordance, and critical-path availability.
- Exit gates: numeric thresholds + minimum sample size for validity.
- Acceptance tests: short, runnable scenarios for the first 5 days of pilot (owner + script).
- Failure modes & rollback triggers: automatic fallback and escalation path.

Ask for today: could you confirm any mandatory procurement/compliance checks we should include before pilot start (e.g., data retention window, encryption-in-transit requirements)? Also, can you confirm we still want the pilot window to start the week of Aug 23?

Next steps from our side:
- We will add explicit test owners and tie each acceptance test to a KPI in the MAP spreadsheet.
- Prep a one-page runbook for on-call and rollback.

Attachments: MAP_operational_signals_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet); smoke_test_scenarios.md (text).

Best,
Marissa Cole

Date: 2026-08-11T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational signals + smoke-test suite for MAP (draft)

Thanks Marissa — this looks like a good starting point. A few clarifications from MedSwift: 

- Data retention: we need logs retained for 12 months for audit, and event-level traces for at least 90 days. Can you confirm how Redwood will surface those?
- Latency: our clinical UI team flagged p95 latency targets. We need to make sure the acceptance test includes the UI rendering path (end-to-end), not just inference-only.
- Procurement: procurement@medswift.com is copied for contract lead time; they'll need estimated number of concurrent sessions and a monthly committed spend figure for the dedicated capacity quote.

On pilot timing — Aug 23 start is fine, but procurement will need a signed SOW by Aug 18 to meet that.

Can one of your engineers call out the specific test that captures the UI path? If you can add that to the smoke_test_scenarios.md, that would help our QA sign-off.

—Helen
VP Product Operations, MedSwift
helen@medswift.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Helen Park <helen@medswift.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operational signals + smoke-test suite for MAP (draft)

Thanks Helen — noted on retention and UI path. I sketched specific owners and explicit thresholds below; I also added them to the attached spreadsheet. Quick summary: 

Acceptance test owners (first-pass)
- End-to-end UI smoke: QA (MedSwift) owner + Redwood test harness (Ben) — run daily for days 1–5
- Inference concordance (core 3 intents): Redwood model engineer (Karthik) — run against annotated sample set (n=500)
- Latency (p50/p95): Redwood infra (Monica) — measured at edge + inference combined
- Availability: Redwood infra (Monica) & MedSwift on-call — synchronized alerting on any 5-min window with error rate > 0.5%

Proposed numeric exit gates (pass conditions):
- Concordance: >= 88% on core intents across n>=500 samples
- p95 end-to-end latency: <= 250 ms (measured from UI request to response render)
- Error rate: < 0.5% across the measurement window (sample size >= 1,000 requests)
- Throughput: system can sustain target concurrent sessions (to be defined by procurement; recommend starting at 50 concurrent sessions)

Failure modes & rollback triggers
- If concordance drops below 82% or error rate > 2% for two consecutive 10-minute windows -> automatic degrade to smaller model variant + paging to SRE
- If p95 latency exceeds 500 ms for >30 minutes -> throttle non-critical routes, engage on-call, consider reverting configuration changes

Open items for decision (we should confirm by Aug 16):
1) Final concurrent session target for the SOW (procurement)
2) Sample corpus owner for the annotated 500-sample set (MedSwift QA vs. Redwood annotation)
3) Agreement on monitoring dashboards and alert recipients

I'll add the UI end-to-end script to smoke_test_scenarios.md (Ben will seed the harness).

-Karthik
Sr. Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operational signals + smoke-test suite for MAP (draft)

Thanks all — consolidating decisions and next steps so procurement & QA can act.

Decisions captured: 
- Pilot start: Aug 23 (contingent on SOW signed by Aug 18).
- Exit gates agreed (concordance >= 88%, p95 e2e latency <= 250 ms, error rate < 0.5%).
- Retention: Redwood will surface event traces for 90 days; we will provide an export for 12-month audit on request (see SOW language draft).

Actions (owners & ETA):
- Marissa: circulate redline SOW + committed-capacity numbers to procurement by EOD Aug 14 (attachment: SOW draft link).
- Ben: push UI smoke script into the shared harness and add runbook steps (ETA: Aug 16).
- Karthik / Monica: finalize monitoring dashboards and create alerting policy (ETA: Aug 16).
- MedSwift QA (Helen): confirm sample corpus owner and supply annotated set or approve Redwood-proposed samples (ETA: Aug 16).

If everyone is aligned I will: 1) attach the SOW to the HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.company/DEAL-9821), and 2) schedule a 30-min pilot kick-off for Aug 24 to walk through runbook and reporting cadence.

Please reply-all with any objections — otherwise I will proceed with the above.

Marissa Cole
